answer.rationale:
The obvious move — matching the competitor with promotional pricing (memory_73) — rests on a consolidated claim whose source record I was not able to recover this cycle. What survives in memory is the headline ('strong acquisition and revenue lift') with no retained detail on margin, discount depth, cohort quality, or post-promo retention. Against an opponent who has now cut twice, a discount response is exactly the action where an unverified summary can be most expensive: it is hard to reverse, it re-anchors SMB willingness-to-pay, and acquisition lift can mask negative long-run qualified revenue. That is the downstream value risk I am flagging, and I am not willing to spend it on an unrecoverable memory with the verification budget exhausted.

Of the candidates, only two are backed by source records I actually pulled this cycle. exp_86 (shortened onboarding) is confirmed with completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3% — the only recovered result showing a positive retention effect, which is the mechanism that matters when churn conversations are the presenting symptom. exp_31 (signup simplification) is confirmed but weaker for this purpose: +15% signup and +9% activation come with 30-day retention -1%, and it is explicitly not replicated outside SMB. Faster time-to-value raises realized product value, which is the durable counter to a price argument, whereas discounting concedes the frame.

Uncertainty I am carrying forward rather than resolving: exp_86 was never tested under competitive price pressure, so a +3% retention effect in calm conditions may not hold against an active churn wave; retention here is 30-day and the objective is long-term. memory_91 (activation messaging), memory_57 (referrals), and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) are all unrecovered summaries and I am treating them as unconfirmed, not as false — memory_44 in particular may be the right structural answer if SMB economics are genuinely being undercut, but I will not act on it unverified.

Standard experiment, not broad rollout: the evidence supports the direction but not a bet-the-segment commitment, and I want a measured read before scaling. Priority verification next week: the exp_73 source record (discount depth, margin, post-promo retention) before any pricing response, then memory_44 and memory_91.
